column4: The section's root ش ف ع includes joining another as a supporter and asking on their behalf; this ayah says whoever makes a good شَفَاعَةٍ shares in its benefit, giving that social sense directly.

The section's dictionary gloss for ش ف ع describes joining another as نَاصِرًا لَهُ; oppressed men, women, and children here ask for a وليّ and نصير to rescue them, making that support a concrete plea for the vulnerable.
The section's shafʿ image is one person joining another as a supporter; here those followed disown their followers at judgment and their ties are cut, reversing that imagined support.
The section says no one can stand beside a person against God's judgment; here the weak ask their former leaders whether they can avert any of God's punishment, and the leaders cannot.

The section pairs neglect of the orphan with failure to urge food for the poor; this ayah frames repelling the orphan and not urging the poor's food as the conduct of one who denies Judgment, while 107:2–3 detail the acts.
The section says creation is paired; this continuation begins God's distribution of daughters or sons as He wills, and 42:50 specifies both sexes together or barrenness.

The section describes created things as paired; this ayah says God may pair sons and daughters or make a person barren, marking a boundary on what pairing means for each family, after 42:49 names one-sex outcomes.

The section says each person comes فَرْدًا, alone; this resurrection scene says souls are paired (زُوِّجَتْ). The pairing's referent is uncertain, so it offers a specific possible reversal of solitary arrival.
The section says hoped-for supporters will not join people at judgment; after 2:166 shows leaders disowning followers, this ayah has followers wish they could return and disown them in turn.
The section's image of failed support is echoed when Satan says he cannot answer his followers' calls and they cannot answer his; 14:21 first shows them asking leaders to avert punishment.
The section says no advocate can match God's judgment; after the worshipped beings deny leading their worshippers in 25:17–18, this ayah says they can neither avert punishment nor help themselves.
The section ends with the soul entering among عِبَادِي; after the recompense statement, this ayah exempts God's sincere servants, and the following verses describe their provision and welcome.
The section turns solitude into belonging among God's servants; this promise names عِبَادِيَ الصَّالِحُونَ as a collective who inherit the earth.

The section ends with a soul joining God's servants; this ayah names the prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous as the company of those who obey God and His Messenger, and calls them excellent companions.
The section's gloss connects entering among God's servants with joining His party; this ayah names Satan's party as the defeated opposite, whose members forgot God's remembrance.
